**Short answer:** Yes – you can file a noise‑complaint in Atlanta, but it’s not the city council that takes the initial call. The complaint is handled by the City of Atlanta’s **Noise Control Division** (within the Department of Public Works), and you can also use the city’s 311 system or online portal to submit it. If you want the issue brought before the city council, you can do so after the complaint has been filed, or you can contact your council representative directly to request that the matter be discussed at a council meeting. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Step | What to Do | Where / How | |------|------------|-------------| | 1 | **Gather details** – Note the exact address, time(s) of the noise, description of the source (e.g., construction, party, loud music), and any evidence (photos, audio recordings). | N/A | | 2 | **Call 311** – Dial **311** (or 404‑656‑4000 if you’re outside the city) and ask for a “noise complaint.” The operator will route you to the Noise Control Division. | Phone: 404‑656‑4000 | | 3 | **Use the online portal** – Visit the City of Atlanta’s 311 website and fill out the “Noise Complaint” form. You’ll need to provide the same details as above. | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 | | 4 | **Email** – If you prefer email, send a detailed message to **noise@cityofatlanta.org**. Include the same information as in the phone or online submission. | Email: noise@cityofatlanta.org | | 5 | **Visit in person** – You can also stop by the City Hall (City Hall Plaza, 1000 Peachtree St NE, Atlanta, GA 30308) during business hours to file a complaint in person. | City Hall, 1000 Peachtree St NE | ### What Happens Next? 1. **Investigation** – The Noise Control Division will schedule a site visit (usually within 7–10 business days) to measure decibel levels and verify the complaint. 2. **Enforcement** – If the noise violates the city’s ordinance (e.g., exceeds 70 dB during daytime or 60 dB at night, or occurs outside permitted hours), the city can issue a warning, a citation, or a fine. 3. **Follow‑up** – You’ll receive a written notice of the outcome. If you disagree, you can appeal through the city’s administrative process. --- ## Relevant Noise Ordinance (Key Points) | Issue | Details | |-------|---------| | **Allowed decibel limits** | 70 dB (daytime 7 a.m.–11 p.m.)
60 dB (nighttime 11 p.m.–7 a.m.) | | **Permitted hours** | 7 a.m.–11 p.m. for most residential areas; 11 p.m.–7 a.m. only for certain commercial zones. | | **Construction** | Must be scheduled between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m.; no work after 7 p.m. unless a special permit is obtained. | | **Music & parties** | No loud music or parties after 11 p.m. in residential neighborhoods. | | **Penalties** | Fines range from $50 to $500 per violation, depending on severity and repeat offenses. | *Full text of the ordinance:* https://www.atlantaga.gov/sites/default/files/2023-04/Noise%20Ordinance.pdf --- ## Bringing the Issue to the City Council If you feel the noise problem is systemic or you want the council to take a broader action (e.g., stricter enforcement, new zoning rules), you can: 1. **Contact your council representative** – Find your district and representative here: https://www.atlantaga.gov/council. - Call or email them to request a meeting or to have the issue added to the agenda. 2. **Attend a council meeting** – Meetings are held monthly (usually on the first Tuesday of the month). Agenda items are posted on the council website. - Bring your complaint documentation and speak during the public comment period. --- ## Quick Reference | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | City of Atlanta 311 | https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 | | Noise Control Division (Phone) | 404‑656‑4000 | | Noise Control Division (Email) | noise@cityofatlanta.org | | Noise Ordinance PDF | https://www.atlantaga.gov/sites/default/files/2023-04/Noise%20Ordinance.pdf | | City Council Contact | https://www.atlantaga.gov/council | --- ### Bottom line - **Yes, you can file a noise complaint** – use 311, the online portal, or email. - **The city council isn’t the first point of contact**, but you can involve them afterward if you want policy changes or broader enforcement. Feel free to let me know if you need help drafting an email or filling out the online form!
